questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

Medical researchers indicated that drinking too many sugary drinks is bad for health. Government intervention to impose a tax on the sale of sugary drinks might help solve which market failures? negative negative over- externalities of externalities of consumption of consumption production demerit goods

options.A: no yes yes
options.B: yes yes no
options.C: yes no yes
options.D: yes no no

questions.questionText: A government uses a cost–benefit analysis approach to infrastructure projects. It is considering building a new railway to link a city centre to its airport. It estimates the following. $ billion private costs 1.0 social costs 1.7 private benefits 0.5 external benefits 1.8 What should the government decide and why? decision reason

options.A: do not proceed total costs exceed external benefits
options.B: do not proceed total costs exceed total benefits
options.C: proceed private costs exceed private benefits
options.D: proceed social benefits exceed social costs

questions.questionText: A consumer currently consumes 10 units of good X and 10 units of good Y at point Z on an indifference curve. The consumer’s marginal utilities from consuming both good X and good Y are positive. Which combination of good X and good Y could be on the same indifference curve as point Z? units of units of good X good Y
The diagram shows two indifference curves and two budget lines for goods X and Y. The consumer’s initial equilibrium is point R. good Y Y Y S IC R IC O X X
What are the correct formulae for calculating average cost (AC) and average revenue (AR)? AC AR TC TR

options.A: key MC MR MC = marginal cost TC
options.B: P  Q MR = marginal revenue P P = price TC TR C Q = quantity Q Q TC = total cost TC TR
options.D: TR = total revenue Q P

questions.questionText: What is always present in monopolistic competition and perfect competition in the long run?

options.A: average revenue = average costs
options.B: average revenue = marginal revenue
options.C: average costs = marginal costs
options.D: average costs = marginal revenue

questions.questionText: A firm maximises its profits by maximising its total revenue. What does this imply?

options.A: Average fixed cost is zero.
options.B: Average revenue is equal to average cost.
options.C: Marginal cost is zero.
options.D: Marginal revenue is greater than marginal cost.

questions.questionText: What will happen to an industry’s supply curve if firms leave the industry?

options.A: It will shift to the left at any given price.
options.B: It will shift to the right at any given price.
options.C: There will be a downward movement along the supply curve.
options.D: There will be an upward movement along the supply curve.

questions.questionText: Which characteristic of a market is a reason for a firm to remain small?

options.A: The minimum efficient scale is high.
options.B: The potential for x-inefficiency is high.
options.C: There are significant economies of scale.
options.D: There is limited access to financial capital.

questions.questionText: What is an example of the principal–agent problem?

options.A: the disincentive effect for entrepreneurs of high government tax rates
options.B: the existence of a trade union to put forward workers’ views to managers
options.C: the lack of consumer knowledge of the quality of firms’ products
options.D: the separation of the owners of a firm from the firm’s managers

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm in imperfect competition. AC MR AR = D MC $ O RS T U quantity It changes its objective from profit maximisation to revenue maximisation. What effect will this have on the firm’s output?

options.A: decreases from T to R
options.B: decreases from U to T
options.C: increases from S to T
options.D: increases from S to U

questions.questionText: Which statement explains why a government decides to increase the highest rates of tax on personal income?

options.A: It expects total tax revenue to be unaffected by the policy change.
options.B: It is concerned about the possibility of emigration by some high earning individuals.
options.C: It regards equity considerations as being more important than efficiency ones.
options.D: It wishes to switch the emphasis of its tax system from direct to indirect taxation.

questions.questionText: In certain countries benefits are provided to individuals on low income. As their income rises the benefits are reduced and income tax has to be paid. What can result from this?

options.A: price stabilisation
options.B: poverty trap
options.C: replacement ratio
options.D: unemployment trap

questions.questionText: An economy requires large inputs of steel for its building programmes. After political pressure, the government imposes a minimum price on imported foreign steel. When would this intervention lead to economic inefficiency?

options.A: when it encourages domestic steel producers to achieve economies of scale
options.B: when it prevents dumping of low-grade steel
options.C: when it protects jobs of highly productive steel workers
options.D: when it reduces competition for steel workers

questions.questionText: What happens to economic rent and transfer earnings if the supply of labour becomes perfectly inelastic?

options.A: economic rent decreases; transfer earnings increase
options.B: economic rent decreases; transfer earnings stay the same
options.C: economic rent increases; transfer earnings decrease
options.D: economic rent stays the same; transfer earnings decrease

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect of the introduction of a minimum wage (W ) in the labour market. M wage rate S L W M W L D L O Q L quantity of labour When would such a minimum wage be least beneficial to workers who are currently employed?

options.A: if demand for the product increases
options.B: if the elasticity of demand for the workers were high
options.C: if the elasticity of supply for the workers were high
options.D: if the productivity of the workers were to increase

questions.questionText: Which statement about economic growth is not correct?

options.A: Economic growth creates costs as well as benefits.
options.B: Long-term economic growth is measured by calculating the percentage increase in GDP for one year.
options.C: Short-term economic growth can be represented by a shift from a point within a production possibility curve to a point on the curve.
options.D: Sustainable economic growth is growth that does not reduce the resources available to future generations.

questions.questionText: Why is real GDP per head thought to be an imperfect measure of welfare in developed economies?

options.A: frequent government manipulation and misuse of data
options.B: no account is taken of inflation
options.C: the restricted scope of the data’s content and coverage
options.D: the shadow economy is greater than the official economy

questions.questionText: What changes are most likely to reduce the level of income inequality in an economy?

options.A: additional government regulation of product and factor markets
options.B: increased progressive direct taxation and decreased indirect taxation
options.C: increased trade union power and reduced labour market flexibility
options.D: reduced welfare benefits and increased rate of interest

questions.questionText: The table gives labour market statistics for Malaysia for January to March 2019. number of people employed 15m unemployed 0.5m not available for work 7m population of working age 23m What is the size of Malaysia’s labour force?
What would encourage industrial expansion in a region of high unemployment?

options.A: a rationing system for building development in that region
options.B: an increase in taxes on investment
options.C: a requirement that only local labour may be employed
options.D: an end to nationally negotiated wage rates

questions.questionText: An island economy has a small manufacturing base, limited mineral resources and limited agricultural land. Which development is most likely to lead to sustainable growth?

options.A: building larger fishing boats to allow fishermen to enjoy economies of scale
options.B: clearing rainforest to create agricultural land for the production of much needed foodstuffs
options.C: training farmers and agricultural workers in new production methods to increase crop yields
options.D: using its domestic mineral resources to give a rapid increase to manufacturing output

questions.questionText: The information in the table is taken from a country’s national income accounts. $ income (millions) wages 8000 salaries 7000 unemployment benefit 1000 government pensions 1000 rent 3000 interest 2000 What is the value of national income in millions of dollars?

In a closed economy with no government sector the marginal propensity to consume is 0.6 at all levels of income. There is an increase in private sector investment of $100 million. What will be the increase in national income?

options.A: $60 million B $100 million C $166 million D $250 million

questions.questionText: According to liquidity preference theory, which money balances are responsive to a change in the interest rate? active balances idle balances

options.A: no yes
options.B: no no
options.C: yes yes
options.D: yes no

questions.questionText: The bank cash deposit ratio changed from 5% to 10%. What will be the result?

options.A: Bank deposits will fall by 10%.
options.B: Banks deposits will rise by 5%.
options.C: The credit multiplier will fall by 50%.
options.D: The credit multiplier will increase by 5%.

questions.questionText: In a developing economy, which policy is most likely to increase the rate of economic growth but restrict economic development?

options.A: an increase in the provision of healthcare facilities
options.B: an increase in the school leaving age
options.C: a removal of health and safety regulations
options.D: the promotion of export-led growth

questions.questionText: Which policy is most likely to conflict with a government’s aim of price stability in the short run?

options.A: increasing spending on education and health
options.B: increasing the basic rate of income tax
options.C: limiting wage increases in the public sector
options.D: preventing mergers of large companies

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be an appropriate government action to reduce both a balance of payments current account surplus and the rate of inflation?

options.A: decrease the rate of interest
options.B: devalue the currency
options.C: increase direct taxes
